scope: Initial caption RAQM/FriBiDi guard, two regressions, pinned-action assertion update, listing/preview workflow dependency setup and CAPTION-FONTS.md. No source edits by reviewer.

native_failure.observed: Lines208-221: font_assets.audit calls font.getlength with direction/language; Pillow raises KeyError because libraqm shaping is unavailable. This is a real rendering dependency failure, not a native app-test failure.

findings.problem: Setup exports the loader path before its Python assertion, but later audit/render steps depend on a DYLD_* value persisted through GITHUB_ENV. Apple documents that protected process launches purge DYLD_* environment variables; a protected default shell can remove it before later Python starts. The within-setup check therefore does not establish the environment required by the subsequent steps.
evidence: Listing capture installs/checks RAQM inside setup, then invokes later Python rendering in a separate run step without re-exporting the loader path.
Preview capability assertion is in setup; its following font audit and later preview renderer are separate steps relying on the persisted DYLD value.
Apple SIP runtime documentation explicitly describes dynamic-linker environment variable purging. This review has no evidence establishing the current runner SIP/shell protection state.
findings.minimal_fix: Persist the Homebrew FriBiDi directory in an ordinary environment variable and explicitly assign/export DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH inside each audit/render step immediately before Python, or use a common launcher that sets it before exec. Preserve strict RAQM checks. Verify a fresh later-step Python process can load RAQM on the actual runner.

positive_assessment: Official Pillow installation documentation requires a separate FriBiDi install for macOS wheels. Homebrew installation plus a loader search path before Python starts is consistent with this requirement; the remaining issue is cross-step persistence.

Every caption measurement passes direction/language, including Latin. Making caption_font reject missing RAQM before font selection correctly closes the old Latin-only gap and turns it into a clear caught audit failure.
Two new tests meaningfully check that missing shaping prevents Latin font selection and appears in the audit failure report. They do not claim macOS dynamic-library loading has executed.

The stale upload-artifact@v4 test becomes a40-hex pinned official-action check while preserving surrounding credential/artifact/native/permission contract assertions. Current workflow pins remain separately reviewed.

No shaping fallback, glyph/font/hash gate, native capture validation, complete asset coverage requirement, privacy/source gate or release_ready status is relaxed. ffmpeg version output uses sed instead of head under pipefail, avoiding an avoidable producer SIGPIPE.

independent_verification.check: Ruby YAML parsing of all workflow files

limits: No macOS Homebrew/Pillow dynamic-library loading or actual final asset render was executed on this Windows reviewer. Current runner SIP state is not assumed either enabled or disabled.
46 Windows tests and parsed YAML do not replace hosted capability checks and actual all-locale caption/image/preview execution.
